newsitem.title: THAILAND: Wu says Bangkok transit project in Thais' hands.
newsitem.headline: Wu says Bangkok transit project in Thais' hands.

text.p: Hopewell Holdings Ltd chairman Gordon Wu said on Tuesday the fate of his company's much-delayed $3.2 billion Bangkok mass transit project was in the hands of the Thai government.

"Unless they act quickly we will not see this process ready for the (1998) Asian Games. The ball is definitely in the Thai government's court," Wu told reporters after speaking to a meeting of international business leaders.
The project financing, including a $100 million syndicated loan from Thai financial institutions, was ready to be drawn down as soon as the Thai government agreed to terms, Wu said.
"The Thai banks' commitment to this is very good. But we want to know the enthusiasm of the Thai government," Wu said.
Last week a Hopewell official said it was looking at equity funding of about $1.0 billion and project financing of over $2.0 billion for its mass transit project.

Executive director Robert Niem told a news conference in Hong Kong on Friday the company was planning to put in the extra equity over the next 12 monhts. He also said the financing would take at least several months to finalise.
Hopewell Thailand will see its registered capital increased to 30 billion baht from 12 billion baht by the end of this year, Wu said, providing terms are agreed to by the government.
Wu said terms regarding fare structure, land acquisition and technical designs were expected to be discussed soon by the Thai cabinet.

Hopewell won a 30-year concession to build and operate a mass transit system in Bangkok from the Thai government in 1990 but wrangles between Hopewell and state agencies overseeing the project have led to serious delays.
